providers.description: AMO Spa sits on Jl. Pantai Batu Bolong No. 69 in Canggu, Kuta Utara, in the middle of the Batu Bolong restaurant strip and within easy reach of Berawa and Pererenan. The business describes itself as a spa and recovery bathhouse, and says it has grown over 18 years from a boutique spa into one of the area's larger wellness addresses. That history matters if you are choosing between the many small salons nearby: AMO operates at a scale where several services sit under one roof. The treatment menu is broad rather than experimental. Massage covers Balinese, deep tissue, hot stone and aromatherapy, plus reflexology and head and shoulder work. Couples can book side-by-side rooms, which the spa confirms on its own site, and the team also runs facials and skin treatments aimed at longer-term results rather than a single glow. What distinguishes the property is the non-treatment side. Guests can move between a plunge and sauna circuit, a massage and the on-site café without leaving the building, which suits a half-day visit rather than a quick appointment. Hours are 08:00 to 22:00 daily. Booking is available through the spa's own booking page or by phone on +62 811 3999 806, and walk-ins are accepted when a therapist is free. Prices vary by treatment and duration and are published on the spa's website; check the current menu before booking, since package pricing differs from single treatments. Payment, cancellation and children's policies are set by the spa, not by this directory.
providers.answer_block: AMO Spa is a spa and recovery bathhouse on Jl. Pantai Batu Bolong in Canggu, open daily from 08:00 to 22:00. The menu covers Balinese, deep tissue, hot stone and aromatherapy massage, reflexology and couples treatments, with a bathhouse and café in the same building.

providers.description: Espace Spa Bali has been operating on Jl. Batu Mejan in Canggu since 2002, which makes it one of the longer-running day spas in an area where venues open and change hands quickly. It sits on the Canggu beach road side of Batu Mejan, within walking distance of Batu Bolong beach. The menu is organised by treatment family rather than by package. The signature is a 'Traditional Oriental' full-body massage that combines long strokes, deeper muscle work and foot reflexology. Softer Swedish-style work is listed as 'Calm and relax me'. A separate Tension Relief set covers deep tissue for the full back, the neck and shoulders, or the lower back only, which is convenient if you want a short, targeted session rather than a full hour. Pregnancy massage, four-hands massage, warm stone massage and crystal aromatherapy foot reflexology are also on the menu, along with the Royal Javanese Mandi Lulur scrub and bath ritual. The spa also teaches: private back-massage classes are offered to individuals and small groups, and the same site sells portable and fixed massage tables and chairs. That side of the business is unusual for a Canggu day spa and is worth knowing if you want to learn rather than be treated. Opening hours are 10:00 to 21:00 daily. Bookings can be made on the spa's booking page or by phone and WhatsApp on +62 361 907 7442 and +62 811 389 0442. Menu prices are in IDR and a 15% government tax is added at payment, so the total differs from the listed price.

providers.description: Fajar Bali Spa occupies a walled tropical garden on Jl. Pantai Batu Bolong No. 22 in Banjar Canggu, a short walk from Batu Bolong beach and the cafés that surround it. The layout is the main selling point: treatments happen in open-air pavilions around a garden rather than in a sealed, air-conditioned block, and the site describes 38 treatment spaces spread across the property. The business now runs two distinct areas: a long-standing traditional Balinese spa and a newer wellness space on the same site. Guests can choose the more rustic garden setting or the newer rooms, which is useful if one person wants a basic massage and another wants a longer package. The massage menu is straightforward and priced by treatment, then by duration. Medical massage starts at IDR 310,000, VCO and aromatherapy at IDR 330,000, shiatsu at IDR 420,000, and four-hands or massage-and-scrub combinations at IDR 450,000. Alongside massage the spa offers facials, manicures, pedicures, waxing and hair treatments such as creambath, so it functions as a general beauty salon as well as a massage spa. Opening hours are long, from 09:00 to 23:00 every day, which makes it a realistic option after dinner. Appointments and package enquiries go through the contact form on the spa's website; no phone number was published on the pages checked, so confirm by form or in person. Prices are quoted in Indonesian Rupiah and exclude any tax added at payment.

providers.description: Kupu Kupu Mas Spa is a day spa on Bali's southern coast in Jimbaran, about a kilometre from Jimbaran Beach and roughly five kilometres from the airport, in the stretch surrounded by the large Jimbaran resorts. It works as a stop on the way in or out rather than a destination spa: the menu is a long list of Balinese-style packages, most of them two to four hours, that string together foot bath, massage, scrub, milk polish, cream bath, flower bath and a drink. Massage on its own is simple and priced flat: Balinese, aromatherapy, acupressure and Ayurveda are all IDR 500,000 for 60 minutes, reflexology is IDR 450,000, stone massage is IDR 850,000 for two hours, and a natural Indonesian facial is IDR 450,000. The two-hour body rituals start at IDR 900,000, the three-hour packages are IDR 1,250,000, and the four-hour Shirodara, King, Queen and Bali Paradise packages are IDR 1,500,000 each. Because the packages carry the value, this is a spa to book as a half-day rather than for a single hour. The spa publishes its menu and prices in English and Japanese. One practical point: no street address or opening hours are published on the pages checked on 31 October 2026, so call the landline or WhatsApp number to confirm both, and ask what tax is added to the menu figure.
providers.answer_block: Kupu Kupu Mas Spa is a day spa in Jimbaran, about a kilometre from Jimbaran Beach. A 60-minute Balinese, aromatherapy or Ayurveda massage is IDR 500,000, reflexology IDR 450,000, and two- to four-hour ritual packages run from IDR 900,000 to IDR 1,500,000.

providers.description: Berkat SPA is a day spa on Jalan Benesari in Kuta, a side street off the main beach strip, and it opens daily from 11:00 to 23:00. The building is a purpose-built spa rather than a hotel facility, with treatment rooms set back from the street, and the spa says it uses organic oils and fresh ingredients prepared on site. The menu covers the standard Bali range plus a few extras: Balinese and aromatherapy massage, warm stone, shiatsu, Thai, deep tissue and four-hand massage, ear candle therapy, an aloe vera treatment aimed at sunburn, and nail, hair and facial work. Prices are published as from-prices in Indonesian rupiah, and they rise with duration: a relaxing full body massage is IDR 130,000 for 60 minutes, IDR 180,000 for 90 and IDR 240,000 for two hours, aromatherapy and shiatsu are IDR 170,000, warm stone is IDR 180,000 for 60 minutes and IDR 225,000 for 90, Thai massage is IDR 180,000 for 60 minutes and IDR 250,000 for 90, four-hand massage is IDR 260,000, and ear candle therapy alone is IDR 80,000. The spa asks for at least two hours' notice for a booking and runs a shuttle within the Kuta and Seminyak boundary. Booking is by WhatsApp or email. It is a walk-in-friendly, mid-priced Kuta option rather than a resort spa, and the page checked on 31 October 2026 did not state whether tax is added, so ask for the total before you commit.

providers.description: Taman Air Spa runs its treatments in a private spa villa on Jalan Sunset Road in Kuta, a short drive from the airport and from the beach strip, and it opens daily from 10:00 to 23:00. The menu is built around long rituals rather than quick massages: most entries run 120 to 240 minutes and combine massage, scrub, mask, bath and a drink, so a visit is closer to an afternoon than an appointment. Prices are printed on the spa's own menu in Indonesian rupiah and include tax and service, which is worth knowing in Kuta where many venues add tax at the desk. The a la carte side is short and clear: a 90-minute Balinese massage is IDR 650,000, hot stone and herbal massage are IDR 825,000 for 120 minutes, shirodara head and back massage is IDR 750,000 for 75 minutes, and facials start at IDR 495,000. Packages start at IDR 850,000 for a 120-minute ritual and reach IDR 2,300,000 for the couple's wine spa. The spa describes its therapists as certified Balinese therapists working in the villa, and it publishes the printed menu alongside the web list so the two can be compared. Booking goes through WhatsApp or the contact page, and the menu states that prices can change without notice, so confirm the figure when you book. If you want a 60-minute massage and nothing else, the a la carte list here is deliberately small.
providers.answer_block: Taman Air Spa is a private spa villa on Jalan Sunset Road in Kuta, open daily from 10:00 to 23:00. Treatments run 75 to 240 minutes with tax and service included: a 90-minute Balinese massage is IDR 650,000 and ritual packages start at IDR 850,000.

providers.description: Bali Orchid Spa runs traditional Balinese spas in two locations, Kuta and Nusa Dua, and this record covers the Nusa Dua branch on Jl. Pratama in Benoa. The two branches are separate businesses for practical purposes, so check which one you are booking before you set off. The model is straightforward: a menu of around twenty treatments built on traditional Balinese massage, with body scrubs, Shirodhara and multi-treatment packages around it. Traditional Balinese massage is listed at IDR 480,000 but sold at IDR 385,000 for 60 minutes when booked direct, and the spa advertises up to 25% off direct bookings across the menu. Packages start around IDR 680,000. Reading the direct price against the list price is worth doing, because the difference is larger than the tax you would pay elsewhere. The Nusa Dua branch sits on Jl. Pratama in the Benoa resort strip, which makes it accessible from the large hotels in Nusa Dua and Tanjung Benoa without a long drive. The spa also markets a wide range of package combinations, so it suits guests who want a scrub, massage and bath in one appointment rather than a single treatment. Opening hours and a single contact number for the Nusa Dua branch were not published in a form that could be confirmed on 31 October 2026, so call ahead through the contact page before travelling. Prices are in IDR and the discounted direct rates apply online, not necessarily at the door.

providers.description: Sari Day Spa is a neighbourhood day spa on Jalan Batur Sari in Sanur, the kind of place local residents use weekly rather than a resort spa attached to a hotel. It opens every day from 09:00 to 21:00, with the last appointment at 19:30, and bookings are taken on WhatsApp. Massage is the core of the business and the prices are modest for Sanur. Balinese massage is IDR 195,000 for 60 minutes and IDR 295,000 for 90 minutes. Deep tissue is aimed at guests who want firm, slow pressure on deeper muscle layers, and the Sari Signature Relaxing Massage is a gentler, rhythmic treatment at the same price as Balinese. Hot stone, foot massage and foot reflexology complete the massage menu; foot treatments start at IDR 165,000. What makes the spa practical is the rest of the menu. Body scrubs and masks, manicures and pedicures with OPI and gel polish, and a hair salon offering cuts, blow-dries, creambath and hair masks all run alongside the massage rooms, so a family or couple can book different things at the same time. There is also a separate kids' menu, which is unusual in Bali and useful for parents. Products are Sensatia Botanicals, a Bali-made brand, and the spa publishes its full price list page by page rather than quoting on request. The site gives the street as Jalan Batur Sari; confirm the exact number on booking, along with current prices, since menus change.

providers.name: Karsa Spa
providers.price_notes: Prices are as displayed on the spa's own menu.
providers.description: Karsa Spa is a Balinese spa in Bangkiang Sidem, in the rice-field country north-west of central Ubud. It is not a hotel spa and does not pretend to be one: treatments happen in open pavilions surrounded by a lotus pond, plants and water, and the property is built with bio-septic tanks so waste does not run into the surrounding fields. The spa states it recycles through Eco Bali and cleans with natural soap nut liquid. The signature treatment is deep tissue, priced at IDR 260,000 for 60 minutes and IDR 380,000 for 90 minutes. The spa describes it as a thorough massage based on Chinese acupressure points to release tension, which is a different experience from the long, oiled strokes that most Ubud menus lead with. Classic Balinese massage is available at IDR 240,000 and IDR 350,000. There is also an Intuitive Heart Massage that begins with Reiki, plus stand-alone Reiki sessions and multi-treatment packages. Oils are Ayurvedic and organic, and the spa names Nadi's Herbal as its supplier because the products are made locally. Karsa Kafe is on the same site, so a massage can be combined with lunch or a juice; the spa notes that sunsets from the property are worth timing a visit around. Getting there is the main practical consideration. Bangkiang Sidem is a scooter or taxi ride from central Ubud rather than a walk, and the lane narrows as it climbs, so arrange the return trip when you book. Opening hours and a phone number were not published on the pages checked on 31 October 2026, so confirm both before setting out.
providers.answer_block: Karsa Spa is a Balinese spa in Bangkiang Sidem, Ubud, known for a deep tissue signature massage priced from IDR 260,000. It also offers Balinese massage, Reiki-based bodywork and spa packages, and sits next to Karsa Kafe, so lunch can follow the treatment.

providers.description: Mekar Ubud is a spa built into the greenery north of central Ubud, arranged as a two-storey main building plus five private 'cocoon' treatment rooms with views into the jungle. It is at the higher end of the Ubud market: massages start at IDR 850,000 per person before tax and service, several times the price of a simple street-side salon, and the setting is what the money buys. Single treatments include the Bali Harmony Massage at IDR 850,000, an Aromatic Candle Massage at IDR 900,000, Prenatal Therapy at IDR 970,000, Deep Tissue at IDR 1,120,000 and Hot Stone at IDR 1,230,000, all priced per person for the shorter duration, with longer sessions at higher rates. Separately, the spa sells cocoon treatments designed as a private ritual for two, which is the format most couples book. The approach is described as Balinese-inspired and 'farm to spa', using natural ingredients in personalised programmes rather than fixed routines, and the property also retails its own product line. If you want a standard 60-minute Balinese massage at a low price, this is the wrong venue; if you want a quiet, private room and a longer ritual, it is a reasonable fit. Opening hours are 09:00 to 21:00 every day. Front desk contact is +62 818 0218 5888 or by email. Prices are marked '++', so tax and service charge are added at payment and the final bill is higher than the menu figure. The site does not publish a full street address, so confirm the meeting point when booking.
providers.answer_block: Mekar Ubud is a jungle-view spa in Ubud with private cocoon rooms for two and single treatments, open daily from 09:00 to 21:00. Massages such as Bali Harmony and hot stone are priced from IDR 850,000 per person, before tax and service.

providers.price_notes: Multi-hour packages are listed on the spa's site between roughly IDR 673,000 and IDR 1,656,000 depending on branch, treatment and duration, with a 10% happy-hour discount on two-hour-plus treatments between 09:00 and 13:00.
providers.description: Sang Spa Ubud has two branches in Ubud: the original on Jl. Jembawan No. 13B in the centre of town, and Sang Spa Tropical on Jl. Raya Pengosekan to the south. The spa states it was established in 2007 and describes its approach as 'farm to spa', with treatments built around organic ingredients and a philosophy drawn from Tri Hita Karana, the Balinese principle of balance between people, nature and the spiritual. Massage options include traditional Balinese, a longer 'Full Body Relief' session, hot stone, stand-alone Balinese reflexology and a four-hands treatment sold as 'Good Karma'. Body scrubs, masks and flower baths are available on their own or inside multi-hour packages, and couple packages such as 'Purifying Balinese Couple' and 'Balinese Self Healing' are listed on the site. Two practical details are worth knowing. First, a daily happy hour from 09:00 to 13:00 gives 10% off treatments of two hours or more, so a morning booking is cheaper than the same treatment in the afternoon. Second, the branches do not always carry the same treatments, so confirm availability for the location you want before travelling. Opening hours are 09:00 to 22:00 daily at both branches. Bookings are handled by WhatsApp, on +62 812 4611 3339 for Jembawan and a separate number for Pengosekan, or by email. Prices are in IDR and package rates, not single treatments, are what the site displays most prominently.
providers.answer_block: Sang Spa Ubud is a spa on Jl. Jembawan in central Ubud, established in 2007, with a second branch in Pengosekan. It offers Balinese massage, reflexology, hot stone and a four-hands 'Good Karma' treatment, open daily from 09:00 to 22:00.

providers.name: Ubud Traditional Spa
providers.price_notes: Prices are per person and marked '+' on the spa's menu, which indicates tax is added. Longer durations and reflexology add-ons are priced separately.
providers.description: Ubud Traditional Spa is a family-run spa in Ubud built around four signature massages rather than a long menu. That focus is the reason to consider it: each treatment is priced per person and can be extended with reflexology or combined with a body scrub and flower bath. The Bali Traditional Massage is the entry point at IDR 280,000 for 60 minutes and IDR 400,000 for the longer session, using palm pressure with long, sweeping strokes, and the therapist sets pressure from gentle to strong on request. The Rice Farmer Massage, at IDR 310,000 for 60 minutes, works the same territory with forearm and elbow pressure for guests who want something firmer. The Ubud Royal Massage is the top of the range at IDR 520,000 for 60 minutes and IDR 760,000 for the longer version, performed by two therapists at once. Balinese reflexology is available on its own at IDR 260,000. Couples are treated together in the same room for any massage or spa programme, which the spa states explicitly. Opening hours are 10:00 to 21:00 every day with the last appointment at 20:00, and the spa closes for Nyepi, Galungan and Kuningan, so check the Balinese calendar around those dates. Booking is by phone or WhatsApp on +62 877 6158 4407, or by email. Prices are marked '+' on the menu, meaning government tax is added at payment. A street address is not published on the site, so ask for directions and pickup options when you book.
providers.answer_block: Ubud Traditional Spa is a family-run spa in Ubud with four signature massages, from the IDR 280,000 Bali Traditional Massage to the two-therapist Ubud Royal Massage at IDR 520,000. It opens daily from 10:00 to 21:00 and treats couples in the same room.

providers.name: LOA SPA Uluwatu
providers.address: Jl. Raya Uluwatu, Ungasan, South Kuta, Badung, Bali 80361
providers.price_notes: The spa states that prices include tax and service, which is not the norm in Bali; most venues add tax at payment.
providers.description: LOA SPA Uluwatu is a Balinese day spa on Jl. Raya Uluwatu in Ungasan, on the Bukit peninsula south of the airport. It describes itself as combining traditional Balinese healing with modern comfort, with private treatment rooms and a stated policy of female therapists, which some guests specifically look for. The menu is short and priced clearly. Balinese massage is IDR 300,000 for 60 minutes, the signature massage starts at IDR 310,000, deep tissue at IDR 330,000, and a 90-minute head and foot massage at IDR 300,000, all for the shorter duration shown with longer sessions priced higher. The spa states that these prices include tax and service, so the amount on the menu is the amount you pay. That is worth noting because many Bali spas quote a figure and add 15% or more at the desk. Private rooms for two make it a workable couples stop, and spa baths are available alongside massage. Opening hours are long, 09:00 to 23:00 every day, which suits a late session after a beach day or a flight into Denpasar. Booking is by WhatsApp: guests send the treatment they want and the spa replies with available times. The spa does not publish a full street number on the pages checked on 31 October 2026, so confirm the exact location and parking before setting out. Ungasan is spread out and taxi drivers do not always know small spas by name.
providers.answer_block: LOA SPA Uluwatu is a Balinese day spa in Ungasan, Uluwatu, open daily from 09:00 to 23:00. Massage starts at IDR 300,000 for 60 minutes with tax and service included, and rooms for two are available for couples.

providers.name: OAZA Uluwatu
providers.address: Raya Uluwatu 88x, Ungasan, South Kuta, Badung, Bali 80362
providers.price_notes: All prices are per person in IDR and exclude any tax the spa applies. Every treatment includes a choice of aromatherapy oil and tea afterwards.
providers.description: OAZA Uluwatu sits on Raya Uluwatu 88x in Ungasan, on the main road that runs across the Bukit peninsula, and is open every day from 10:00 to 23:00. It is a massage and facial spa rather than a resort spa: pricing is transparent, walk-ins are welcome, and there is no minimum spend or pool-day format. Massage starts at IDR 235,000 per person for the shortest session, with deep tissue, Lomi-Lomi, four-hand and hot stone options above that; hot stone is IDR 510,000 for 90 minutes. Foot reflexology with a scrub starts at IDR 210,000 and is a sensible choice after a day of walking the Uluwatu clifftop paths. The spa also runs a thermal therapy treatment from IDR 275,000, which combines heat with bodywork. The most complete option on the menu is the Uluwatu Signature, a 130-minute session combining a full-body massage, a signature facial and a footbath for IDR 600,000 per person. Facials appear on the same menu without a published price on the page checked on 31 October 2026, so ask when booking. Two details stand out. Every treatment includes a choice of aromatherapy oil and tea afterwards, and the spa states that prices are per person and any tax is added at payment. Phone and WhatsApp are +62 811 3940 4241. The spa publishes its full menu with prices on its own site, so compare before you commit to a package sold elsewhere on the island.
